It's Monday, 7 a.m. Your alarm goes off. But it doesn't sound like your alarm.
You open your eyes. The ceiling is wrong. The bed is huge. And there's a tie hanging on the door.
You walk to the mirror. And your dad is staring back at you.
Oh no. Oh no, no, no.
Across the hall, someone screams. It's you. Well, your body. With your dad inside.
Why am I so short? Why does this room smell like socks?
In the kitchen, your mom takes a sip of coffee. And makes the worst face you have ever seen.
This is disgusting. How do you drink this every day?
Give me that. And why are my legs so short?
Somehow, overnight, everyone swapped. You got Dad's life. Dad got yours. Mom and your sister switched too.
So, what if you swapped lives with your parents for a week?
Okay, rules. It lasts exactly seven days. Next Monday at 7 a.m., everything goes back.
You have to live their life completely. Their job. Their school. Their bills. Their problems.
And nobody outside this house can know. If anyone finds out, the swap becomes permanent.
Permanent? I am not doing sixth grade math again.
Relax, Dad. How hard can school be?
He gives you a long look. With your own face.
